items.title: Billy Mitchell interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995
items.q: we had a rehearsal one time in Chicago, and Nelson Riddle brought in material for an album. And we rehearsed it and ran it down

ctx.x: Do you think it’s because those guys knew exactly what went well in the band, because they were right in the middle of it so they could write more effectively?

Yeah. They could write for the people in the band. Like when one of them wrote something, he envisioned, he knew the capabilities of the person he was writing it for. I’ve seen, to give you an example, we had a rehearsal one time in Chicago, and Nelson Riddle brought in material for an album. And we rehearsed it and ran it down, and naturally the first time with things like that, Nelson was listening and thinking about some things he could change. And then Marshall said, “Thad did you say you had something?” And…
No kidding. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -8-
